title: Correct wave speed(s)
description: Essential: The response must give the correct numerical wave speed(s) (54 m/s for positive direction, 58 m/s for negative direction) for part (1).

title: Correct propagation direction
description: Essential: For part (2), the response must state the wave propagates in the negative x-direction.

title: Identifies possible phase shifts
description: Important: The reasoning must consider both possible propagation directions (positive and negative x) leading to different phase advances (e.g., 3λ/8 or 5λ/8).

title: Applies time interval constraint
description: Important: The solution must correctly use the inequality 3T < Δt < 4T to determine the integer k (k=3) for the phase shift.

title: Relates speed, wavelength, period
description: Important: The final calculation must correctly use the relationship v = λ / T, with λ=8 m and T derived from Δt = kT + (phase fraction)T.

title: Determines wavelength from graph
description: Optional: The student may explicitly note that the wavelength λ is 8 m, as read from the provided waveform figure.

title: Direction from speed comparison
description: Optional: For part (2), the student may show that comparing the given speed (74 m/s) to the calculated speeds determines the direction.

title: Sign or unit error
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the final answer has incorrect units (e.g., m/s) or a sign error in the direction statement.

title: Misinterprets phase shift
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the student assumes only one propagation direction or misidentifies the phase shift (e.g., uses λ/2 instead of 3λ/8 or 5λ/8).
